heard: Sitting Bull saw soldiers falling before they even arrived. In June 1876, George Custer approached the little bighorn. His scouts warned him the village was too massive. He ignored them, unaware General Crook had already retreated. Custer split his force to stop them escaping. His final note begged for help that never arrived. Over 200 men were wiped out in an hour. Sitting Bull's vision of falling soldiers had come true.
